name: Diabetes Mellitus Type 2
description: A metabolic disorder characterized by high blood sugar, insulin resistance, and relative lack of insulin.
prevention: Diet rich in fiber and whole grains, low in refined sugars
reference: American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes

name: Essential (Primary) Hypertension
description: Persistently elevated arterial blood pressure without an identifiable secondary cause, defined as systolic BP >= 130 mmHg or diastolic BP >= 80 mmHg.
prevention: DASH diet (rich in fruits, vegetables, low-fat dairy)
reference: ACC/AHA Guidelines for High Blood Pressure in Adults

name: Acute Coronary Syndrome / Myocardial Infarction
description: Acute ischemia of myocardial tissue resulting from acute coronary artery occlusion by atherosclerotic plaque rupture and thrombosis.
symptoms: Radiation to left arm, shoulder, jaw, or neck
prevention: Strict blood pressure and glucose control
reference: ACC/AHA Guidelines for the Management of Patients With STEMI / NSTEMI

name: Bronchial Asthma
description: A chronic inflammatory disorder of the airways characterized by variable and recurring symptoms, reversible airflow obstruction, and bronchospasm.
risk_factors: Exposure to airborne allergens (dust mites, pollen, pet dander)
treatments: Short-Acting Beta Agonists (SABA e.g. Albuterol) as rescue
reference: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Global Strategy for Asthma Management and Prevention

name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
description: Infection of the pulmonary parenchyma acquired outside of hospital settings, causing alveolar consolidation and impaired gas exchange.
symptoms: Productive cough with purulent or rust-colored sputum
Pleuritic chest pain (worse with deep breaths)
treatments: Empiric antibiotics (e.g. Amoxicillin, Macrolides, Respiratory fluoroquinolones)
reference: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) / ATS Guidelines on CAP

name: Ischemic Stroke
description: Focal neurological deficit caused by sudden occlusion of a cerebral blood vessel resulting in cerebral infarction.
treatments: Intravenous thrombolysis (IV Alteplase / Tenecteplase within 4.5 hours)
Mechanical thrombectomy (within 6-24 hours for large vessel occlusion)
reference: AHA/ASA Guidelines for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke

name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
description: A condition which develops when the reflux of stomach contents causes troublesome symptoms and/or complications into the esophagus.
prevention: Avoid lying down for 3 hours after eating
Avoid chocolate, peppermint, caffeine, fatty foods, and citrus
treatments: Laparoscopic Nissen fundoplication in refractory cases
reference: ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of GERD

name: COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2)
description: An infectious respiratory illness caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2).
symptoms: Sudden loss of taste (ageusia) or smell (anosmia)
prevention: Wearing high-filtration masks (N95/KN95) in crowded indoor areas
reference: NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines / WHO Guidelines

name: Migraine
description: A neurological condition characterized by recurrent, disabling, unilateral pulsating headaches accompanied by nausea, photophobia, and phonophobia.
prevention: Identification and avoidance of dietary and environmental triggers
Preventive medications: Beta-blockers, Topiramate, CGRP antagonists
treatments: Rest in a quiet, dark room
reference: American Headache Society (AHS) Guidelines for Migraine Management

name: Osteoarthritis
description: Degenerative joint disease involving progressive degradation of articular cartilage, subchondral bone remodeling, and secondary synovitis.
symptoms: Joint aching pain worsening with weight-bearing activities
Joint effusion and reduced range of motion
risk_factors: Joint injury or repetitive occupational stress
prevention: Maintain healthy weight to reduce mechanical load on knees and hips
treatments: Intra-articular corticosteroid or hyaluronic acid injections
Total joint replacement (arthroplasty) for advanced disease
reference: ACR / Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis
